source.title_on_document: Towards AI as Colleagues: Multi-Agent System Improves Structured Ideation Processes

supplement.where: Appendices A to D at the end of this PDF
supplement.holds: questionnaires, the GPT-5 originality and pragmatic-style scoring prompts, system prompts; no additional outcome statistics

paper_design_summary: Twenty participants (15 students, 5 early-career professionals) each brainstormed a self-chosen problem for about 10 minutes with MultiColleagues, a multi-agent GPT-4o system with AI personas, and with ChatGPT (GPT-4o) as a single-agent baseline, in randomly assigned counterbalanced order. Outcomes were self-rated outcome quality and novelty, GPT-5 originality scores of the conversations, and GPT-5-coded topic branching and noun-based concept production in participants' own contributions. There is no no-AI arm.

studies.label: Within-subjects user study (MultiColleagues vs ChatGPT baseline)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two conditions (MultiColleagues first or ChatGPT baseline first); every participant used both systems on the same self-chosen problem
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of two condition orders, with equal distribution across sequences to control order effects.

arms.name: MultiColleagues
arms.description: Multi-agent conversational system on GPT-4o: user selects AI persona colleagues, explore/focus modes, AI facilitator

arms.name: Baseline (ChatGPT)
arms.description: ChatGPT web interface using GPT-4o, unrestricted text-based ideation on the same problem

participants.who: 15 undergraduate to PhD students (computer science, information science, HCI, AI, communication) and 5 early-career professionals in technology, research, and design; recruited through university mailing lists and professional networks; aged 20-39
participants.quote: our study recruited 20 participants through university mailing lists and professional networks (9 males, 11 females), aged 20-39 years (M = 26.7, SD = 3.8).
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 4.1 and Table 2 (P1-P20); t(19) tests on p. 12, Section 5.3.1

ai_tool.name_model: MultiColleagues (multi-agent system on OpenAI GPT-4o) versus ChatGPT web interface with GPT-4o
ai_tool.how_used: Free conversational brainstorming with the AI for about 10 minutes per condition, think-aloud, ideas recorded in a Google Doc

task.description: Brainstorm solutions to a self-chosen ideation problem (same problem in both conditions)
task.duration: about 10 minutes per condition, extendable; session about 70 minutes in total

outcomes.name: Idea originality (TTCT-inspired, GPT-5 judge)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-5 rated each participant's full conversation on a 5-point originality rubric, three runs averaged; not validated against human raters (p. 18, Section 6.6)

contrasts.reported: MultiColleagues M = 3.78, SD = 0.38 vs Baseline M = 3.59, SD = 0.44; W = 70.0, p = .202

outcomes.name: Topic branching ratio in participants' contributions
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-5 segmented each user contribution into main topics and sub topics (three runs averaged, two researchers checked, kappa = 0.86); ratio = sub topics / main topics.

contrasts.reported: MultiColleagues M = 6.45, SD = 2.54 vs Baseline M = 3.50, SD = 1.79; t(19) = 5.15, p < .001

outcomes.name: Perceived Quality & Novelty (self-reported)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Post-system survey items Q5 and Q7 on 7-point Likert scales; the abstract's headline result; does not satisfy criterion 3

contrasts.reported: MC 5.95 ± 0.92 vs Baseline 4.97 ± 1.16; W = 17.0, p <.01, effect size r = 0.69

outcomes.name: Concept production rate in participants' contributions
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Nouns extracted from each participant's own contributions using a natural language toolkit; nouns serve as a proxy for concept introduction, reported as concepts per minute (p. 9, Section 4.3.3; p. 12, Section 5.3.1).

contrasts.reported: MultiColleagues M = 2.05 concepts/min, SD = 0.81 vs Baseline M = 1.26, SD = 0.67; t(19) = 2.59, p < .05

eligibility.reason: Randomized within-subjects experiment (random order of a multi-agent GPT-4o system vs a ChatGPT baseline, an ai_design comparison) with 20 participants analyzed (p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 8, Section 4.2), well below 50. Output-scored outcomes exist (GPT-5 originality of the conversations, topic branching), so criteria 1 and 3 are met; the paper goes to the screening report as a small randomized experiment.

one_line_finding: With 20 participants, no statistically significant difference in GPT-5-scored originality was detected between MultiColleagues and ChatGPT (3.78 vs 3.59, W = 70.0, p = .202, pp. 12-13), while topic branching (6.45 vs 3.50, t(19) = 5.15, p < .001, p. 12) and self-rated quality and novelty (5.95 vs 4.97, p < .01, Table 6) were higher with MultiColleagues.
